**Why it was a problem:** Every frontend module's remote entry embedded its own copy of `@module-federation/runtime-core`. The runtime is identical across modules, so each app downloaded the same code again on every page load. The changeset puts the cost at about 85 kB raw (about 26 kB gzipped) per production remote entry on `@openmrs/esm-login-app`, of which the runtime is most of the size. The fix's goal is that "a page downloads it once rather than once per app." (`openmrs-esm-core/.changeset/mf-runtime-shipped-once.md:8-14`)

**What the app shell does now:**

- At startup, `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/index.ts:5-7` calls `publishFederationRuntime()` before anything else.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/federation-runtime.ts:30-42` publishes the error-code and SDK helpers on globals (`_OPENMRS_FEDERATION_ERROR_CODES`, `_OPENMRS_FEDERATION_SDK`). It logs an error if `_FEDERATION_RUNTIME_CORE` is missing, which is the runtime the shell itself provides through `experiments.provideExternalRuntime`.
- The shell's `openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/rspack.config.js:489-502` sets `provideExternalRuntime: true` and `optimization: { target: 'web' }`, so the shell's copy of `runtime-core` is the only one.
- Remotes built by `openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/rspack-config/src/index.ts:471-542` use `experiments.externalRuntime: true` and map `@module-federation/sdk` and `@module-federation/error-codes` to those globals. The `@module-federation/runtime` and `webpack-bundler-runtime` packages stay bundled per remote, because a shared copy would hit RUNTIME-010 (`index.ts:527-530`). The changeset says about 14 kB of runtime stays per remote.

**Change and ticket:** The change is the commit "(feat) Federate most of the Module Federation runtime (#1853)" (`04f538d`). It is the only commit that touches the changeset file. The changeset itself names the ticket as **O3-5873** ("Ship the Module Federation runtime once, from the app shell"). The commit message does not name a ticket, so the link to O3-5873 comes from the changeset.

**Compatibility cost:** This is a breaking change. Remotes built with the new tooling need an app shell of the same version or newer, and they refuse to start under an older one. Webpack-built remotes also grow (about 8.7 kB to 23 kB raw), because they previously shipped no runtime at all. The changeset covers both points (`mf-runtime-shipped-once.md:16-29`).

I did not read the commit diff itself, so the sizes come from the changeset text and not from a build I checked.

Single-spa uses the location referenced by the `route` or `routeRegex` to determine the pages that get rendered into that location via the `getActivityFn` function. Pages in O3 are essentially single-spa applications with a predetermined `<div>` tag that they get rendered into. Extensions leverage the single-spa `parcel` concept - they have the exact same lifecycles as single-spa applications, except that they don't have a `getActivityFn`. This means single-spa will never automatically mount or unmount a parcel. Instead, you have to manually tell it when to mount or unmount a parcel. The extension system exists to determine when an extension should be loaded (and subsequently invoke the `mount` function on it) and unloaded (and subsequently invoke the `unmount` function on it). Every extension is mounted through the `Extension` component defined in the framework. This component essentially renders the extension (by invoking single-spa's `mount` function) and unmounts the parcel when the component is unmounted. It defines a `<div>` with a `data-extension-id` property into which React renders the parcel. The key thing to note about pages and extensions is that once `<div>`s get created for them, React takes over and renders the page or extension into the DOM.
